walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Hasselt' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140049)
walls.note: Hasselt town wall (13th c., four gates; rebuilt several times, replaced by an earthen rampart only in 1705), traced from the Ferraris map (1777), whose wall line follows the medieval one. Wet moat all round. Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south).

landmarks.footprintNote: tower height today incl. 18th-c. spire; 1650 height not verified
landmarks.y1650: Main parish church of Hasselt (13th-15th c.) with its west tower, the town's main bell tower; not yet a cathedral (bishopric 1967).
Chapel of Our Lady with the Virga Jesse statue (14th c.), goal of the septennial Virga Jesse procession; the present baroque church dates from 1728-42, so in 1650 a smaller Gothic chapel stood here.
Hall built c. 1400, used as meat hall, later cloth hall and council house (inventory 140049); position on the Grote Markt not verified.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Hasselt' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140049)

landmarks.y1650: Second beguinage, inside the walls on the Nieuwe Demer from 1571 (the present buildings are of 1707 onward).
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Hasselt' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140049)

landmarks.y1650: Town refuge of the Cistercian abbey of Herkenrode, built 1542-44.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Hasselt' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140049)

landmarks.y1650: Massive gatehouse with ravelin, drawn in 1687.

ruler.name: Prinsbisdom Luik
ruler.sovereign: Prince-bishop Ferdinand of Bavaria (1612-50), then Maximilian Henry of Bavaria (elected 1650); neutral in the Franco-Spanish war (neutrality recognised by Spain only in 1654, see history-check F76)
